predecessors.name: Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd
predecessors.text: the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd, unified and renamed the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on 23 September 1932

ledger.x: 1932: Ibn Saud proclaims the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on 23 September, uniting Hejaz and Nejd.
November 1933: the Yemenis advance on Najran.
14 June 1934: the Treaty of Taif ends the war.
14 June 1934: Najran, Asir and Jizan become Saudi.
7 July 1934: the last Saudi troops leave Yemen.
1936: Cliopatria's Saudi shape takes in the Rub' al Khali.
31 August 1952: Saudi guards enter the Buraimi oasis.
25 October 1955: British-led forces retake the oasis and the Saudis are flown out.
25 October 1955: the fighting over the oasis ends with the British retaking it.
9 August 1965: Jordan's coast on the Gulf of Aqaba grows.
25 July 1966: the Saudi-Kuwaiti neutral zone is partitioned.
1982: the Saudi-Iraqi neutral zone is partitioned.

wars.name: Saudi-Yemeni war
wars.outcome: Saudi victory in 87 days (20 March to 14 June 1934): the Treaty of Taif made Jizan, Asir and Najran Saudi with 'temporary sovereignty' renewable every 20 years; Saudi forces returned Hodeida and Hajjah and the last left on 7 July.

wars.name: Buraimi dispute
wars.outcome: Saudi guards occupied Hamasa on 31 August 1952; arbitration in Geneva collapsed in 1955 and British-led forces took the oasis on 25 October 1955; the oasis was split between Oman (Buraimi, Hamasa) and Abu Dhabi (Al Ain); the dispute was settled by the Treaty…

wars.name: Gulf War
wars.outcome: Saudi Arabia condemned the invasion of Kuwait in 1990 and its forces took part in 1991 'in bombing raids on Iraq and in the land invasion'; no Saudi border changed.

certainty.note: The Jordan frontier follows the Hadda agreement of 2 November 1925 and is sharp; the Taif frontier with Yemen was a partial border drawn in 1934 and demarcated over two years; the neutral zones and the whole Rub' al Khali frontier with…

Sharp on the Jordan frontier from the treaty of 9 August 1965, on the Kuwait neutral-zone line from 1966-1970 and on the Iraq line from 1982; the Oman, UAE, Qatar and Yemen frontiers across the desert stay soft (the UAE frontier of 1974…
The Oman border is sharp after the treaty of 21 March 1990 (demarcation finished in 1995); the Yemen frontier rests on the Taif treaty and the memorandum of 26 February 1995 and stays soft.
The Treaty of Jeddah of 2000 'finalised the entire border' with Yemen; the UAE frontier of 1974 remains disputed.
